title: Deserialization guard is a single funnel in sklearn loader; test both flag states for each format
answers: where is the pickle deserialization check enforced for sklearn models
add a new serialization format to mlflow sklearn loader
test that the deserialization flag blocks and allows a model load
pyfunc load of skops model should respect MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION
body:
Invariant: every sklearn model load (mlflow.sklearn.load_model and pyfunc.load_model, which both route through the same loader) must pass the MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION check in mlflow/sklearn/__init__.py:_load_model_from_local_file before any format-specific deserialization. Adding a format or early-return branch above this check reopens the bypass.
What breaks if skipped: a model with an attacker-controlled allow-list or pickle payload executes code on load while the user believes the flag protects them.
Convention in tests/sklearn/test_sklearn_model_export.py: a guard test should cover both the blocked state (flag 'false', asserting both mlflow.sklearn.load_model and pyfunc.load_model raise) and the allowed state (flag 'true', the same loads succeed), so an inverted condition fails the test.
Constraints: the Databricks runtime and model-serving carve-outs intentionally skip the check; tests run outside those environments.
applies: Changes to sklearn model loading or to new loaders in the same area; does not cover the save path.
says: Untrusted model loading protection is bypassed when opening certain saved model formats.
Models still load executable code despite the security setting disabling unsafe deserialization.
Enforce the unsafe model load block consistently across all model formats.
Ensure disabling unsafe deserialization strictly blocks loading untrusted model artifacts.
search: Every scikit-learn model load via mlflow.sklearn.load_model and pyfunc.load_model must funnel through the MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION check in mlflow/sklearn/__init__.py:_load_model_from_local_file before format deserialization. The Databricks runtime and model-serving environments intentionally bypass this check. Tests in tests/sklearn/test_sklearn_model_export.py must verify both the blocked flag state ('false') raising errors and allowed state ('true') succeeding across formats.
